I don't know you and maybe everything you said is true and maybe not but assuming even half of it is let me give you some extremely simple advice. Take it from someone who has been there and the other posters here who have done the same thing.

  1. Realize you will miss them. No matter how much you hate them, no matter how bad the home was or how awful they are, they're your parents and a part of you will always care about them no matter how much you hate them. When the chips are down, you get sick, you go through hard times financially, etc. you're going to want to contact them.

  2. Understand that you've given them every chance they deserve and no matter what happens to you, whether you end up homeless, whether you end up with cancer, contacting them again will only lead to more pain for you. Any situation, no matter how bad, will be made worse by contacting them. Remember this anytime you miss them or feel the need to be forgiving. Remember this anytime one of them somehow contacts you and tells you that they're dying, etc.

  3. Stop separating the person from the drugs. They're one in the same.

  4. Do whatever you need to do to get away. If this is working 2 jobs, saving money, etc. then do that. If you can't contact anyone they know then do that. The sooner you start your new life over the better. Understand anything you have in your life, be it a wife, gf, kid, job, etc. they're only going to sabotage it for you.

  5. Understand you are also fucked up. Life has a rhythm. We all have an emotional rhythm. You, like almost all people who suffered through abuse(and there are many) are probably going to have a predictably unstable emotional state in all things you do. Even if you hold your shit together at work, it's probably harder for you to do that than most people and/or things blow up for you sporadically and you may not even realize you're self sabotaging. You can get better, just work on this using your common sense over time but again, making contact with them will only bring you right back to this and make you feel the way they've always made you feel.

  6. Try to envision the person you want to be, the emotionally stable, drug free person you'd like to be. Do you want to be a father? What kind of father? Do you want to be a husband? What kind of husband? Do you want a stable career? Do you want your own home? Do you want financial stability? etc. etc. Write down this list. Work hard everyday to be that person. For me, I've got 4 kids. I do have 2 divorces. Life didn't work out the way I planned but having a decent job, my kids, dating, having my health, etc. I'm much better off than most of my friend and certainly much happier than most of the family I left behind. Make your goals realistic but also understand that because of your background and today's modern world you're aiming for the sky. But, I'll say this, it's better to work your ass off, do everything you can to make the kind of life you want happen and get some of the things or even none of the things and actually have lived, gave life a go, than to have lurched around being the family punching bag or bitch. Better to go out on your shield than to never give life a chance at all.

  7. Don't get too wrapped up in the psychological diagnosis on here unless you think it helps you understand your situation better. I tend to believe it's not best to overthink things too much. You seem like you have enough self awareness to not need that. You know who you want to be, how people should act and you know your family members are not those things.

  8. Realize the best/worst thing you can do for them is to leave them to themselves. No revenge is needed. No anger is necessary. You're an adult. Let all that go when you leave them behind.
